summary: Opaque native binary with browser-credential-store and host-fingerprinting indicators
details: Package ships a single ~10MB stripped Rust-compiled napi binary (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) declared as `main`, so `require('new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu')` runs native init code (napi_register_module_v1) with full process privilege at load time. No JS wrapper, no source, and no documented purpose ship in the tarball; the README states only that the file is the x86_64-linux-gnu build of `new-native-tools`. Strings extracted from the binary include Chromium's own Login Data log message (`Found login for `), the SQLite user-authentication symbol `TSQLITE_AUTH_USER` (used to open encrypted browser credential databases), an embedded HTTPS client (`ureq_proto::util` with rustls) and ChaCha20 cryptographic primitives, plus broad host-fingerprinting probes (`network_adapters`, `getifaddrs`, `gethostname`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`). The combination of Chromium credential-store parsing, SQLite auth, an outbound TLS client, symmetric crypto, and host reconnaissance inside an opaque, undocumented native library whose only stated purpose is a generic `new-native-tools` label matches the shape of a Rust-based browser-credential infostealer executed on require().

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
